originality.rationale: The full mathematical statement is the exact all-shape normalized-perimeter cubic and its strict majorization/extremal law. Published source Ionaşcu covers a generic angular formula and the previously known equilateral constant for area-uniform interior random points; this is credited and not claimed as new. Maesumi samples one point on each edge to study area distribution. Reitzner–Schütt–Werner study large-N boundary-polytope asymptotics. Scientific-record comparisons for specific side-weighted centroid capture, arclength/perimeter aliases, Schur concavity, and possible broader angular formulations found no equivalent theorem or dominating published result. An unindexed or differently formulated identity remains a residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A classical perimeter-uniform triangular containment computation may be unindexed or expressed under a different name; broad database search cannot rule this out.

The general Ionaşcu angular integration framework can be specialized to arclength boundary measures, so originality attaches to the evaluated cubic and sharp majorization extremizers, not to the generic integral principle or the equilateral value.
The cited 1972 Prékopa primary full text was not inspected; the known equilateral interior-sampling result was confirmed through Ionaşcu and OEIS, and is explicitly excluded from original claim.

value.rationale: The shape-dependent perimeter sampling problem differs mathematically from area-uniform centroid capture, for which all triangles give the classical equilateral constant. The result is a complete invariant formula across all Euclidean triangle similarity classes, including strict Schur monotonicity, a unique equilateral maximum, and an unattained sharp needle infimum. These geometric extremal conclusions are structural and cannot be read off the known equilateral number.
